summary: A 2–6 m many-stemmed shrub with flexible flood-bent shoots and adventitious roots. It colonizes moist riverbanks and gravel bars, but regular seasonal fruiting is restricted to channels whose roots retain year-round groundwater access. Fruit draws rondo and dense stems conceal merodeador (F8, F11, F18, F21).

links: Runoff alternately buries and exposes channel-side stems.
Buried living nodes root in damp sediment.
Root networks retain gravel and support recovery after partial damage.
chains.play: Follow thickets along freshwater corridors and gather fallen flexible stems.
chains.weakness: Scour removes root mats; prolonged burial or submergence kills shoots, and disconnected bars can dry out.
observe: New roots emerge from buried nodes.
Gravel collects downstream of stem clusters.
Bent survivors produce upright shoots after floods.

plausibility.summary: Flood regeneration permits colonization of seasonal gravel bars without guaranteeing permanent water access or fruit. Marine tides are not the driver.

analogues.mechanism: Flexible shoots, regeneration and adventitious rooting interact with freshwater flow and sediment deposition.

links: Year-round groundwater access sustains fruit development through seasonal drying.
Soft fruit rewards rondo with water and carbohydrates.
Visitors carry surviving seeds beyond the parent thicket.
Seeds establish where moist open sediment persists.
chains.play: Seek fruit-bearing thickets beside groundwater-connected channels; do not expect every shrub strip to carry a crop.
chains.weakness: Groundwater disconnection prevents dependable fruiting; transported seeds often fail on dry or scoured ground.
observe: Soft green-gold fruit hangs over a spring-fed channel.
A nearby seasonal gravel-bar colony remains fruitless.
Rondo leaves seeds on moist openings beyond the thicket.

plausibility.summary: Enable regular fruit production only where roots retain year-round groundwater connection. Water access permits a crop but does not guarantee one; softness and scent indicate ripeness.

analogues.mechanism: Fruit recruits seed carriers, while water supply and deposition sites constrain reproduction and establishment.

gameplay.gift_item: Soft river-fruit cluster from a groundwater-connected thicket

poison.signal: Green foliage; softness and scent identify ripe fruit.

gameplay.cover: Dense stems conceal small creatures and predators.
gameplay.nest_material: Fallen flexible twigs, bark fibres and leaves.
gameplay.notes: Only year-round groundwater-connected patches support regular seasonal fruiting. Fruit does not cure poisoning, shrub presence does not certify potable water, and slender stems do not reliably bear player weight.

relations.note: Visits fruiting groundwater-connected patches and transports seeds.
Forages for associated aquatic greens along open freshwater margins.
Conceals approaches to crossings and fruit visitors.
Forms shrub ribbons through meadow channels, including some seasonal nonfruiting bars.
Shelters ferns in persistently humid bank pockets.
Provides craft material throughout suitable thickets and fruit only in eligible patches.

generator.trunk: Several slender woody stems from a shared crown; old stems arch over deposited gravel.

branching.buttress: Absent; root mats and rooted low branches form the base.

colour.base: Medium green leaves and olive-brown stems
overlay_rules: Eligible ripe fruit becomes soft muted green-gold.
Red is not a fruit-edibility cue.

placement.slope: Freshwater channel margins, moist gravel bars and spring-fed benches.
placement.wetness: Moist rooting sediment permits establishment; regular fruiting additionally requires year-round groundwater connection.
placement.soil: Channel gravel, sand and silt; exclude regularly saline tidal ground.
placement.density: Bank ribbons and bar colonies interrupted by scour; fruiting instances restricted to groundwater-connected patches.

generator.seasonal: Wet periods support growth and resprouting. Late-summer to autumn fruiting occurs only at year-round groundwater-connected sites; other colonies are not reliable fruit sources.
generator.wind_response: Slender stems bow together; floods leave persistent downstream bends.

journal.en: The river bends it and buries it. Fruit stays where its roots keep the water.
journal.es: El río la dobla y la entierra. El fruto queda donde las raíces conservan el agua.
